name: Elite Shooter (sample data)
basedOn: Derived from the basketball-shot-analysis library's pro-form profile heuristics. NOT measured elite-shooter data.

feedback.tooLow: Elbow angle is below optimal range. A tighter 90° angle maximizes force transfer through the shot line.
feedback.tooHigh: Elbow is too extended at set point. Optimal L-shape position creates better backspin and consistency.

shootingElbowAngle.explanation: The bend of your shooting arm at the set point. A right-angle L stores energy and releases it straight up through the ball.

feedback.tooLow: Elbow is over-tucked. While alignment is good, slight natural flare improves comfort and repeatability.
feedback.tooHigh: Excessive elbow flare reduces shot accuracy. Align elbow under the ball for a straighter shot line.

shootingElbowFlare.explanation: How far your shooting elbow drifts out from your body. A tucked elbow keeps the ball on a straight line to the rim.

feedback.tooLow: Abbreviated follow-through indicates incomplete release. Full extension and hold ensures consistent ball flight.

followThroughHold.explanation: How long you keep your arm up after release. Holding it keeps the release smooth instead of jerky.

feedback.tooLow: Incomplete arm extension limits release height and angle. Full extension optimizes release point.

maxArmExtension.explanation: How fully your arm extends on the release. Full extension adds arc and consistent power.

feedback.tooLow: Insufficient wrist flexion reduces backspin and soft touch. Increase wrist snap for better rotation.
feedback.tooHigh: Over-flexion can cause inconsistent release. Moderate snap maintains control while generating spin.

wristSnapAngle.explanation: How much your wrist flexes through the release. A full snap puts backspin on the ball for a soft bounce.

feedback.tooLow: Set point is too low, reducing release height and creating longer ball path to target. Elevate set point.
feedback.tooHigh: Very high set point may affect rhythm and timing. Find optimal height for your mechanics.

setPointHeight.explanation: How high you set the ball before release. A high set point is harder to block and simplifies the release.

feedback.tooLow: Release angle is flat. Increase arc to optimize entry angle into the basket.
feedback.tooHigh: Release angle is too steep. Reduce arc slightly for better distance consistency.

releaseAngle.explanation: The angle of your arm as the ball leaves. Releasing upward gives the shot arc so it can drop softly through.

feedback.tooHigh: Ball dip is slowing shot tempo. Minimize pre-shot movement for quicker, more fluid release.

ballDip.explanation: How far the ball drops before rising. A small, smooth dip builds rhythm without wasting time.

feedback.tooHigh: Lateral ball path deviation affects consistency. Straighter path to set point improves repeatability.

ballPath.explanation: How straight the ball travels from catch to set point. A straight lift is repeatable and quick.

feedback.tooLow: Brief set point may indicate rushing. Slight pause at set point improves rhythm without slowing shot.
feedback.tooHigh: Extended pause at set point slows release. Quicken transition to release phase.

setPointDuration.explanation: How long the ball pauses at the set point. One fluid motion beats a hitch that saps power and timing.

feedback.tooLow: Ball is positioned too far forward. Slight behind-head position creates better shooting angle.
feedback.tooHigh: Ball is drifting too far behind head. This can affect release timing and control.

ballBehindHead.explanation: How far the ball drifts behind your head at the set point. Keeping it forward keeps the motion compact.

feedback.incorrect: Guide hand must be positioned on the side of the ball at elite level. Under or thumb-up positions introduce inconsistency.

guideHandPosition.explanation: Where your off-hand sits on the ball. On the side, it supports without pushing.

feedback.tooLow: Guide hand releasing early may cause loss of control. Maintain contact until optimal release point.
feedback.tooHigh: Late guide hand release can interfere with shot path. Separate hands precisely at release.

guideHandRelease.explanation: When your guide hand leaves the ball. Leaving early means only your shooting hand aims the shot.

feedback.tooLow: Guide arm too tight restricts natural ball support. Allow moderate separation.
feedback.tooHigh: Excessive guide arm flare can pull shot off-line. Maintain controlled position.

guideElbowFlare.explanation: How far your off-hand elbow sticks out. A relaxed guide elbow keeps the guide hand from steering the ball.

feedback.tooLow: Insufficient knee flexion limits power generation. Increase load for better leg drive.
feedback.tooHigh: Deep knee bend slows shot release. Optimal flexion balances power and quickness.

kneeFlexion.explanation: How deep your knees bend before rising. The right bend generates effortless range.

feedback.tooLow: Minimal hip engagement reduces power transfer. Engage hips in the load phase.
feedback.tooHigh: Excessive hip drop slows overall motion. Optimize load depth for speed and power.

hipDrop.explanation: How much your hips lower in the dip. Loading your hips powers the shot from the ground up.

feedback.tooLow: Premature leg extension disrupts ball-leg synchronization. Delay leg drive slightly.
feedback.tooHigh: Late leg extension causes disconnected motion. Start leg drive earlier for fluid power transfer.

legExtensionStart.explanation: When your legs begin extending in the shot. Legs firing first sends energy up the kinetic chain.

feedback.tooHigh: Forward lean exceeds optimal range. Maintain near-vertical spine for consistent balance.

backPosture.explanation: How upright your spine stays through the shot. Staying tall keeps your shot line consistent.

feedback.tooLow: Head tilting away from target affects aim. Keep head level and eyes on target.
feedback.tooHigh: Excessive head tilt toward target can affect body alignment. Maintain neutral head position.

headTilt.explanation: How steady and level your head is. A still head means steady eyes and better aim.

feedback.tooLow: Shoulder rotation away from target reduces accuracy. Square shoulders to basket.
feedback.tooHigh: Over-rotation creates inconsistency. Maintain neutral shoulder alignment.

shoulderAlignment.explanation: How square your shoulders are to the rim. Square shoulders point everything at the target.

feedback.incorrect: Elite shooting requires consistent cup position for optimal ball control and release. Hinge position introduces variability.

handCupVsHinge.explanation: Whether your shooting wrist is loaded back under the ball. A hinged wrist is a spring ready to snap.

feedback.tooLow: Ball rising before leg extension indicates disconnected upper/lower body. Synchronize leg drive with ball lift.
feedback.tooHigh: Leg extension preceding ball rise wastes power. Time ball lift with leg drive initiation.

ballLegSync.explanation: How your ball lift and leg drive line up. Synced timing turns leg power into easy range.

feedback.tooLow: Premature ball rise disrupts loading phase. Allow full lower body load before ball lift.
feedback.tooHigh: Delayed ball rise extends shot time. Initiate ball lift earlier for quicker release.

ballRiseStart.explanation: When the ball starts moving upward in the shot. Consistent timing makes the whole motion repeatable.

feedback.tooLow: Early leg extension before ball rises creates timing mismatch. Coordinate with ball movement.
feedback.tooHigh: Late leg drive results in arm-dominant shot. Initiate leg extension earlier.

legRiseStart.explanation: When your legs begin to rise. Early leg drive leads the shot instead of chasing it.

feedback.tooLow: Early release point indicates rushed shot. Build full rhythm before release.
feedback.tooHigh: Late release extends shot time and reduces effectiveness off the catch. Quicken release timing.

releaseStart.explanation: When the release begins within the shot. Releasing on the way up uses your momentum.

feedback.tooLow: Very fast release may sacrifice consistency. Ensure full mechanics within quick release.
feedback.tooHigh: Extended shot duration creates defensive opportunities. Work on quickening overall motion.

totalShotDuration.explanation: How long the whole shot takes. A compact shot gets off before defenders can react.
